claim_summary: The work combines a master-agent workflow for routing time-series requests, temporal prompt-pool conditioning, and task-specific SLM instruction tuning with preference optimization.

claim_evidence.quote: a novel approach using an agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework for time series analysis to improve task-specific outcomes by addressing challenges like distributional shifts, fixed window limitations in time series data.
leverages a hierarchical, multi-agent architecture where the master agent orchestrates specialized sub-agents and delegates the end-user request to the relevant sub-agent.

modules.name: Master-agent task routing
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK no: the router dispatches requests but does not implement a task-family output objective or verifier; R3_2_GTS no: its dispatch state has no temporal semantics; R3_3_GH yes: it manages delegation and synthesis.

evidence.quote: The master agent for sub-agent orchestration utilizes the ’ReAct’ prompting technique[45], encouraging the general-purpose SLM to think step-by-step and use external tools (sub-agents, each utilizing a fine-tuned SLM for specific time series tasks) to generate responses.
In summary, the master agent orchestrates sub-agents, selects the most appropriate sub-agent, and allocates the task to the specialized sub-agent.

modules.name: Differentiable temporal prompt-pool conditioning
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK no: the retrieved pattern memory is not bound to one task objective; R3_2_GTS yes: retrieval is keyed by temporal-series inputs and historical patterns, so its assumptions depend on temporal data.
rubric_path: R3_2_GTS:yes - temporal input and historical patterns

evidence.quote: The key vector acts as an identifier or query vector to retrieve relevant prompts from the pool based on similarity to the input new data, providing a form of conditioning or context about historical patterns to enhance the predictions.
The selected prompts, along with the original input, are concatenated to form the input embedding

modules.name: Task-specific SLM instruction tuning
modules.scope_reason: R2 assigns parameter-efficient instruction tuning of SLMs to the LLM side because it trains model responses on time-series tasks.

evidence.quote: We perform instruction-tuning of SLMs with an improved context length [19](32K tokens) using parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) techniques on their associated specific tasks (e.g., forecasting, imputation) using the corresponding time-series datasets.
Datasets: We evaluate the proposed Agentic-RAG framework on four tasks: forecasting, classification, anomaly detection, and imputation.

modules.name: Time-series direct preference optimization
modules.scope_reason: R2 assigns DPO to the LLM side because it updates SLM outputs toward preferred task-specific responses; it is separately described and ablated from instruction tuning.

evidence.quote: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO; [32]), which involves randomly masking 50 % of the data and performing binary classification task to predict the corresponding correct task-specific outcomes.

Effectiveness of direct preference optimization (DPO): – We evaluated the framework’s performance with and without DPO and assessed how aligning SLMs with preferred outcomes impacts the accuracy and reliability of predictions.

temporal_validity.quote: We adopted a time-based division strategy to split multiple benchmark datasets into training, validation, and testing sets.

task_performance.quote: For forecasting and imputation tasks, the performance of the proposed framework is evaluated using MAE, RMSE, and MAPE metrics on the original scale of the time series data.

notes: The master workflow is treated as fixed because the described flow selects and calls sub-agents from the user request; returned sub-agent output is synthesized, with no reported experiment showing that tool feedback changes later actions. The dynamic prompt pool is classified as GTS here because its key-value retrieval depends on temporal inputs and historical patterns.
